scope: Accepted target-A DROID wrist-to-exterior LoRA data contracts
summary: The accepted v10 contract provides 91 episode-disjoint target-A training pairs and three heldout pairs; v11 expands each training episode to start/middle/end clips for 273 pairs without changing the heldout episodes.
evidence: v10 contains 91 training examples from 91 training episodes, three heldout examples, and excludes validation episodes 12/20/54/66/91 plus holdouts 21/60/77 and too-short episode 79.
v11 contains 273 training examples from the same 91 training episodes by sampling three deterministic temporal positions per episode.
Both contracts attest episode_disjoint=true, heldout_anchors_used_for_training=false, and heldout_targets_used_for_training=false.
v11 dataset-contract SHA-256 is 673fc86ccd3a0a75165f67f00980ca59b732053de1250d28f7de230583bf22dd and adaptation-manifest SHA-256 is 74e1cd2819aaab73a53db68f9120175138b864b47d158fdd5cf46f41a4098672.
The four v11 transfer archives matched their local SHA-256 values before extraction on a800-2.
Coordinate frames are explicit: camera:wrist_image_left_pixels to camera:exterior_image_1_left_pixels.
lessons: Episode-level holdout is required because temporally adjacent clips from the same robot episode would leak appearance and action state.
One real target-view anchor frame can be disclosed while the synchronized remaining target video stays withheld for post-generation evaluation.
limitations: The data contract validates synchronization and leakage boundaries; it does not imply that a trained model will generalize.
next_actions: Evaluate every trained checkpoint on episodes 21, 60, and 77 with the frozen target-leakage guard.
